subject: Usage backfill & one-time settlement proposal
messages:
From: Sam Carter <sam.carter@netwave.ai>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected May spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Hi Chloe,

Hope you had a good week. We discovered a sizable spike in inference hours against our Dedicated pool for May (see attached summary). This pushed us well past our committed capacity, and the billing for the overage landed on our finance queue this morning.

Before we process payment, can you:
- Confirm Redwood's usage reconciliation for May (raw token/hour breakdown)
- Share any insights on what might have driven the spike (we suspect an internal A/B test)
- Propose options for settlement — ideally something that avoids a large one-off invoice hitting our next billing cycle

Attaching a lightweight export: usage_report_may.csv [attachment stub].

Thanks — Sam

--
Sam Carter
Head of Platform Ops | NetWave AI
sam.carter@netwave.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@netwave.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@netwave.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected May spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for the export, that helps. I've pulled the logs from our serving layer and reconciled the hour-by-hour runs for your pools. High-level:

- Root cause: a staged rollout of a new personalization model triggered longer sequences for a subset of keys between May 11–18, increasing token consumption by ~3.6x for impacted requests.
- Reconciliation result: the attached CSV aligns with our billing data; we have a per-hour breakdown and caller-id mapping if you want it.

Proposal to resolve without a large immediate invoice:
1) One-time bridging credit: Redwood will apply a conditional credit equal to 40% of the overage amount, provided NetWave signs a short amnesty memo acknowledging the spike and committing to a joint postmortem and guardrails plan.
2) Escrowed makegood: The remaining balance can be placed into a 60-day escrow to be amortized against future committed usage (applied monthly until exhausted).
3) Preventative measures: We'll help you pin the model variant and enable per-route token caps for the sensitive routes you identified.

If this approach sounds reasonable, I'll draft the amnesty memo and loop in Finance to set up the escrow instruction. Laura, can you confirm the finance steps for creating the escrow and applying the credit?

Thanks — Chloe

Attachments: reconciliation_notes_may_summary.txt (inline summary)

--
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Sam Carter <sam.carter@netwave.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected May spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Sam / Chloe — finance here. Quick operational notes:

- We can issue a one-time invoice credit for 40% of the documented overage once we have the signed amnesty_memo.pdf on file (PDF signature or DocuSign acceptable).
- For the escrow option, Redwood can create a credit-escrow ledger entry tied to Deal RDW-2027-4532; the remaining 60% will be applied as a monthly credit over the next 3 billing cycles by default, unless you request a custom amortization.
- Timing: credit issuance requires a signed memo and a short PO/email confirming escrow instructions. Once received we can apply the credit to your next invoice (processing lead time 5–7 business days).

Sam — attaching a template amnesty memo and an escrow instruction checklist. If NetWave agrees, send back the signed memo and confirm the accounting contact for the PO.

Attachments: signed_amnesty_memo.pdf (template in this thread), escrow_checklist.docx (stub)

Best — Laura
Finance Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@netwave.ai>, chloe_martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected May spike — need reconciliation and next steps

Appreciate the quick triage everyone. NetWave — happy to approve the 40% one-time credit + 60% escrow amortization as proposed. Two final asks before finance issues the credit:

1) Please sign the amnesty memo and reply with the preferred PO or accounting contact so we can set the escrow.
2) Confirm whether you'd like the amortization applied over 3 months (default) or stretched over 6 months — we can do either.

If you confirm by end of week, I'll flag this for expedited processing so credits appear on your July invoice rather than creating a separate one-off charge.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
